q: A black object is a good absorber and a good radiator whose ____ is close to one. (2024)
e: An ideal blackbody has an emissivity equal to 1, making it a perfect absorber and radiator of radiation.

q: Heat convection is one of the primary ____ of heat transfer. (2024)
e: Convection, conduction, and radiation are the primary modes or processes through which heat transfer occurs.

q: Thermal equilibrium occurs when the systems are at the same ____ difference. (2024)
e: Systems reach thermal equilibrium when their temperatures are equal, resulting in zero net heat transfer.

q: One of the basic requirements for heat transfer is the presence of a ____ . (2025)
e: Heat flows spontaneously from a higher temperature region to a lower temperature region due to a temperature difference.

q: Heat ____ is a transfer of heat that does not require a material medium. (2025)
e: Thermal radiation travels in the form of electromagnetic waves and can propagate through a vacuum without needing a medium.

q: Carnot engine is not ____ efficient. (2025)
e: According to the second law of thermodynamics, no heat engine operating in a cycle can be 100% efficient.

q: The object which can absorb all the electromagnetic radiations falling upon it is called a ____ . (2025)
e: A black body is a theoretical object that completely absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation regardless of frequency or angle.

q: The emissivity of an object depends on the ____ of radiation. (2025)
e: Emissivity is a spectral property that varies depending on the specific wavelength of the emitted radiation.

q: The ____ of an object depends on the wavelength of radiation. (2025)
e: The measure of a surface's ability to emit thermal energy relative to a blackbody is called emissivity, which depends on wavelength.

q: The object which can absorb all the electromagnetic radiations falling upon it is called a ____ . (2025)
e: An object that absorbs 100% of incoming thermal and electromagnetic radiation is classified as a black body.

q: ____ of an object depends to a large extent on how shiny it is. (2025)
e: Shiny or highly polished surfaces reflect light well and consequently have very low emissivity values.

q: The natural process of heat transfer between an object and its surroundings is driven by ____ differences, aiming to reach thermal equilibrium. (2025)
e: A temperature difference drives heat flow until thermal equilibrium is established between an object and its environment.

q: The SI unit of heat flux density is ____ . (2025)
e: Heat flux density represents the rate of heat flow per unit cross-sectional area, measured in watts per square metre.

q: Silver coated object whose emissivity is much ____ than 1. (2025)
e: Silver-coated surfaces reflect nearly all radiation, giving them an emissivity value far below 1.

q: The total emissive power of a blackbody is directly proportional to the ____ power of absolute temperature. (2025)
e: Stefan-Boltzmann law states that the total radiant energy emitted by a blackbody is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature.

q: An ____ process occurs at constant volume. (2025)
e: An isochoric process is a thermodynamic process during which the volume of the system remains constant.

q: The ____ of a system is the sum of the energies of all the constituent particles. (2025)
e: Internal energy includes both the microscopic kinetic and potential energies of all particles comprising the system.

q: An ____ process occurs at constant pressure. (2025)
e: An isobaric process is a thermodynamic transformation in which the pressure of the system stays unchanged.

q: The emissivity of an object depends on the ____ of radiation. (2025)
e: Spectral emissivity measures radiant emission characteristics, which vary as a function of radiation wavelength.

q: A series of processes in which a system is brought back to its initial state is called a ____ . (2026)
e: A thermodynamic cycle involves a sequence of processes returning a system to its initial state.

q: ____ of an object depends to a large extent on how shiny it is. (2026)
e: Surface finish and reflectivity directly influence emissivity; shiny surfaces emit much less thermal radiation.

q: The emissivity of an object depends on the ____ of radiation. (2026)
e: The wavelength of emitted thermal radiation dictates the spectral emissivity value of a given material.
